## Overview

Offline embedding refresh is a scheduled batch process that regenerates vector embeddings for a corpus when either the underlying embedding model changes or source documents update in bulk. Rather than regenerating embeddings on demand at query time, these jobs run on a fixed cadence and atomically swap newly generated vectors into the retrieval index.

## Key Characteristics

**Scheduling and Cadence**

- Runs on a fixed schedule rather than on demand
- Processes the full document set or incremental updates depending on the scope of changes
- Triggered either by model upgrades, bulk document changes, or time-based intervals

**Index Swap Strategy**

- New vectors are generated independently before replacing production embeddings
- Atomic swap ensures no serving of mixed-model results during transition
- Prevents inconsistent retrieval results caused by partial embeddings from different model versions

## Operational Concerns

**Model Versioning**

- Each batch job must be tagged with the embedding model version used
- Enables tracking which production vectors were generated from which model
- Critical for understanding quality changes and supporting rollbacks

**Vector Drift Monitoring**

- Operators must monitor divergence between old and new vectors for the same documents
- Drift detection helps identify whether new embeddings represent meaningful improvements or unintended model behavior changes
- Provides early warning of retrieval quality regressions

**Blue/Green Index Deployment**

- New embeddings are staged in a parallel (green) index before swap
- Production (blue) index remains live and queryable
- If quality regression is detected post-swap, rollback to blue index is straightforward without downtime
- Enables rapid recovery from problematic model upgrades or configuration changes

## Related Concepts

This pattern is part of the broader retrieval system lifecycle and relates to embedding model management, vector database operations, and deployment strategies for machine learning systems.
